newsitem.title: USA: Colts owner Irsay dead at 73.
newsitem.headline: Colts owner Irsay dead at 73.

text.p: Indianapolis Colts owner Robert Irsay, who moved the NFL team from Baltimore under cover of darkness in 1984, died in Indianapolis Tuesday, the football club said.
Irsay, 73, had suffered a stroke more than a year ago. He died at Indiana Medical Centre where he had been admitted Monday.

Irsay, a Chicago native who made a fortune in the heating, ventilating and air conditioning business, gained control of the Colts on July 26, 1972, when he traded his recently acquired Los Angeles Rams for the Colt franchise.

He enraged Baltimore fans by secretly moving the team to Indianapolis in 1984. He hired a moving company pack up the teams's Baltimore offices during the night and fans in that city awoke to find that a franchise associated with the city since 1946 was gone.
Irsay later said his "greatest thrill in football" was being greeted by Indianapolis fans when the team arrived there.

He was survived by his widow Nancy and two sons, Tom, 42, and Jim, 37. Jim Irsay is currently the team's senior executive vice president, general manager and chief operating officer. He was previously vice president and general manager.
